concerns.text: Tasks T215, T216, and T217 mandate implementing experimental validation protocols (Stark-effect spectroscopy) and external benchmarking against physical measurements. This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' principle relative to the Spec (spec.md:Assumptions & FR-011) which explicitly defines 'Physical measurement validation is out of scope' and restricts ground truth to QM9 DFT reference data. These tasks attempt to consume a 'physical measurement' artifact that the spec explicitly states does not exist for this feature.

Tasks T222, T223, and T224 require implementing conformational ensemble sampling (3-5 conformers) and weighted average predictions. This violates the spec's explicit assumption that 'Single lowest-energy conformer per molecule... is used' and that 'ensemble sampling is documented as future work.' The tasks attempt to consume 'conformer ensemble' data that the spec's data model (single conformer) does not produce.

Tasks T211, T212, and T213 introduce physics-informed regularization and specific bond-angle/length filters based on external expert reviews. These tasks depend on a 'physics-informed architecture' artifact that is not produced by the spec's defined Functional Requirements (FR-004 defines a 'lightweight SchNet-style GNN' without these specific constraints). This creates a dependency on a non-existent producer.

Task T032 (Compute MAE/RMSE against QM9 dipole-moment reference values) has an unresolved claim status ('not_enough_info'). This indicates the 'QM9 reference data' artifact required for this consumer task is not yet verified or available, breaking the data-flow dependency chain for US2 evaluation.

Phase 8 tasks are marked [P] (parallel-safe) but depend on the completion of Phase 5 (US3) and Phase 6 (Validation) to establish baselines. While the text notes this dependency, the [P] tag is semantically incorrect for tasks that must wait for specific metric outputs (T032, T040) to be generated. These should not be marked parallel-safe until the baseline artifacts are produced.
